overview: Croatia is a country in south-eastern Europe, on the Adriatic Sea. Its capital and largest city is Zagreb. Croatia was part of Yugoslavia until it declared independence in 1991. It joined the European Union in 2013 and adopted the euro in 2023. Its coastline, islands and old towns such as Dubrovnik and Split make it one of Europe's most popular holiday destinations.

geography.text: Croatia has an unusual crescent shape. The north and east are part of the flat Pannonian Plain, crossed by the Drava and Sava rivers. The long Adriatic coast is lined with more than a thousand islands, with the Dinaric Alps rising just behind it. The Plitvice Lakes, a chain of lakes linked by waterfalls, are among its best-known natural sights.

history.text: Croatia became a kingdom in 925 and from 1102 was joined with Hungary, later becoming part of the Habsburg lands. After the First World War it joined the new state that became Yugoslavia. Croatia declared independence in 1991, fought a war until 1995, and joined the European Union in 2013.

events.title: First king
events.text: Tomislav is crowned the first king of Croatia.

events.title: Union with Hungary
events.text: Croatia enters a union with the Kingdom of Hungary that lasts for centuries.

events.title: Joins a new South Slav state
events.text: Croatia becomes part of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, later Yugoslavia.

events.title: Independence and war
events.text: Croatia declares independence; fighting lasts until 1995.

events.title: Joins the EU
events.text: Croatia becomes the 28th member of the European Union.

government.text: Croatia is a parliamentary republic. The Sabor, its parliament, is elected every four years and chooses the Prime Minister, who leads the government. The President is elected every five years and represents the country abroad. Croatia joined NATO in 2009 and the European Union in 2013, and adopted the euro in 2023.

economy.text: Tourism is the biggest part of Croatia's economy. Millions of visitors come to its Adriatic coast and more than a thousand islands every summer. Shipbuilding, food processing and pharmaceuticals are also important.

culture.text: Croatia gave the world the necktie: Croatian soldiers' scarves inspired the French cravat in the 1600s. Its coast is full of walled stone towns built by Venice and others. Dubrovnik's old town is a UNESCO site and was used as a filming location for Game of Thrones.

items.title: Dubrovnik
items.text: A walled city on the sea, once the rich Republic of Ragusa.

items.title: Diocletian's Palace
items.text: A Roman emperor's palace in Split that people still live inside.

items.title: Plitvice Lakes
items.text: Sixteen terraced lakes joined by waterfalls.

sport.text: Football is Croatia's biggest sport. For a country of under four million people, its team has done remarkably well: runners-up at the 2018 World Cup and third in 1998 and 2022. Croatia is also strong in handball, water polo and tennis.

items.text: Croatia reached the World Cup final, losing 4–2 to France.

items.title: Handball
items.text: Croatia's men won Olympic gold in 1996 and 2004.

didYouKnow: The Dalmatian dog breed is named after Dalmatia, a region of Croatia.
Croatia has more than 1,000 islands, but fewer than 50 are lived on.

keyPeople.name: Nikola Tesla
keyPeople.text: Born in 1856 in Smiljan, in today's Croatia, to a Serbian family.

keyPeople.name: Marco Polo
keyPeople.text: Some say he was born on Korčula, though Venice is more likely.
